Thailand is one of the easiest countries in the world to travel independently, and being connected is a big part of why. From the first taxi out of Bangkok to a longtail boat off Koh Lanta, your phone is what smooths the way: hailing a Grab instead of haggling, reading a street-food stall through your translation app, messaging a guesthouse in Chiang Mai that you are on the later bus. You will want data from the moment you land, and these days you need it even before you arrive.

Here is how to stay connected in Thailand, and why I reach for an eSIM.

A Thailand-specific reason to sort this early

Thailand now requires most arriving travellers to complete a digital arrival card (the TDAC) online shortly before entry, and you also have e-visa and entry systems to navigate. Rules change, so always check the current requirements on official Thai government sites before you fly, but the practical point stands: you increasingly need to be online around your arrival, which is one more reason to sort your connection before you land rather than after.

Your options in Thailand

  • A local SIM is cheap and easy to buy at the airport, but it means a kiosk queue, showing your passport, and swapping out your home SIM on arrival.
  • Pocket wifi is an extra device to carry, charge and return.
  • An eSIM installs on your phone before you leave home and works the instant you touch down; nothing to collect, swap or hand back.

For most travellers, the eSIM is simply the least friction.

Why I use Holafly in Thailand

Thailand is one of Holafly‘s covered destinations, and it gives me exactly what a Thailand trip needs:

  • Online the moment I land, with no airport kiosk, which after a long flight to Bangkok is a small blessing.
  • Unlimited data on the Holafly Unlimited Data eSIM (200+ destinations), so I never ration data when I am leaning on maps, Grab and translation all day, and if Thailand is one stop on a wider Southeast Asia trip, the same eSIM keeps working across the region.
  • Options to suit how you travel: Holafly’s Travel eSIMs let you choose the exact number of days you need for a single trip, while Holafly Plans are a global subscription for frequent travellers and digital nomads who want continuous connectivity across many destinations. And Holafly Always On sits alongside them as a backup, a global data safety net of 1 GB every month across 150+ destinations for the unexpected or the gaps between trips.

Check current plans and prices on Holafly’s site, and remember two honest basics: your phone must be eSIM-compatible, and it is a data plan (you keep your own number on your home line for calls and texts, or use internet calling over the eSIM’s data).

My tips for a connected Thailand trip

  • Install the eSIM before you fly, over home wifi, so it activates on arrival, and so you can complete the TDAC and any entry formalities without scrambling for a signal.
  • Put Grab, Google Maps and a translation app on your phone before you go; they are the trio you will use most.
  • Download offline maps of your areas as a backup.
  • Carry a power bank: a day of navigating and translating in the heat empties a battery fast.

Thailand is made for the spontaneous, the detour, the stall you spot down a side soi, and a phone that just works is what lets you follow it without a second thought. I would not travel Thailand without it.

Frequently asked questions

Do you need an eSIM for Thailand?

You need reliable data, and for most travellers an eSIM is the easiest way to get it. It installs on your phone before you travel and works the moment you land, with no kiosk queue or SIM-swapping, which is handy given Thailand now asks arrivals to complete a digital arrival card (TDAC) online. A local SIM or pocket wifi also work, but with more hassle.

Does a Holafly eSIM work in Thailand?

Yes, Thailand is one of Holafly’s covered destinations. You install the eSIM before you fly and it activates on arrival; the Unlimited Data eSIM covers 200+ destinations, which is useful if Thailand is one leg of a wider Southeast Asia trip. Check the current plans and prices on Holafly’s site before booking.

Can you use one eSIM across Southeast Asia?

Yes, if you choose a multi-destination plan. Holafly’s Unlimited Data eSIM covers 200+ destinations, so the same eSIM can keep you connected as you move between, say, Thailand, Laos and Vietnam, without buying a new SIM in each. Check that each destination on your route is covered before you travel.

When should you set up your Thailand eSIM?

Before you leave home, while you still have wifi. Install and, if possible, pre-configure it so it activates automatically when you land, that way you can complete Thailand’s online arrival formalities and hail a ride without hunting for a signal at the airport.

Silvia Moggia

Silvia Moggia is an Italian travel writer, tourism consultant and boutique hotel owner based in Liguria. She has written the independent travel blog Silvia's Trips since 2013, entirely from first-hand experience, usually travelling solo, on foot, on horseback and under sail. She specialises in independent and solo female travel, responsible and sustainable tourism, overtourism and destination management, the Cinque Terre and Liguria, Northwest Argentina, and Arctic and Nordic winter travel. She owns and runs the Oasi Eco Boutique Hotel in Levanto, writes for the industry journal Officina Turistica, teaches digital marketing for destinations, and is the author of a published guidebook to Northwest Argentina.
